corrected_verdict:
KNOWN. The verdict stands.
- **What the identity is:** a one-line consequence of character orthogonality. The paper does not claim it as a contribution.
- **Single-neuron case, delta-resolved:** n=2 is in Morwani App. F.1; general k is in the proof of Li et al. Lemma D.7.
- **Network-level diagonal reading:** already in Morwani App. F.3 (fhat(j,k,l) > 0 on j = k = -l) and in Li et al. Lemma F.1.
- **Adjacent analogues:** Tian (NeurIPS 2025) Thm 1 is the squared-loss split into diagonal and off-diagonal terms. Kunin et al. (NeurIPS 2025) and Marchetti et al. (ICML 2026) give the delta=0 per-neuron correlation, i.e. the utility.
- **What I did not find anywhere:** the arbitrary-table, all-delta statement, with the off-diagonal part named interference and paired into Re(beta_j)·cov_j. This is a trivial extension and should not be sold.
- **Numerical check:** I verified the formula, including the constant 2p^{-(n+1)} and the product-neuron form, to 1e-16 at (p,n) = (5,2) and (7,3).
issues:
Both confirmed citations exist and say what is claimed; I fetched and read both PDFs. The checker's section pointers need small fixes.

1. **Morwani, wrong equation pointer.** The identity eta~(delta) = p^{-3} sum_j uhat(j)vhat(j)what(-j) rho^{j delta} ("only terms where j+l=k+l=0 survive") is the unnumbered display before Eq. (5). Eq. (5) is the objective and Eq. (6) is the evaluated margin. The cosine/phase form leads to Eq. (7), not Eq. (6). Cite "App. F.1", not "App. F.1, Eq. (5)".
2. **Morwani proof outline overstated.** The Theorem 7 proof outline states only the consequence E[psi'] = 2/((p-1)p^2) sum_{j != 0} uhat vhat what(-j). It does not state eta~(delta) itself.
3. **Li et al., wrong definition pointer.** Def. D.5 defines eta with the power neuron (u1+...+uk)^k w. The product eta~ and its Fourier form appear only inside the proof of Lemma D.7, together with the remark that all monomials except w·prod u_i vanish. Cite "proof of Lemma D.7".
4. **Nanda and Gromov, now read in full.** The checker confirmed these from abstracts only; I read the PDFs.
   - Nanda §4.2 fits the logits to sum_k alpha_k cos(w_k(a+b-c)) with 95% variance explained.
   - Gromov Eqs. (10)-(16) keep only the n+m-q cosine after phase averaging.
   - Neither states the averaging identity, so the checker's characterization holds.
5. **Prior art the checker missed.** All of it is adjacent; none of it is the exact statement.
   - (a) Morwani App. F.3 already takes the whole max-margin network's multidimensional DFT and shows fhat(j,k,l) > 0 when j = k = -l != 0. This is the network-level diagonal-mode precedent, and Li et al. Lemma F.1 copies it. It should be the citation for the network-level form.
   - (b) Tian, NeurIPS 2025 (arXiv 2410.01779), Thm 1 and Lemma 1: the squared-loss objective of quadratic nets on Abelian groups is -2 r_kkk (diagonal, the signal) plus squared off-diagonal r_{k1k2k} terms, which the optimum sets to zero. This is the squared-loss analogue of the paper's diagonal/interference split.
   - (c) Kunin et al., AGF, NeurIPS 2025, §5 / Thm 5.1: the per-neuron utility is (2/p^3) sum_k |xhat|^2 uhat vhat what xhat, which is the delta=0 diagonal correlation.
   - (d) Marchetti et al., ICML 2026 (arXiv 2602.03655), App. B Lemmas B.1–B.2: the k-fold group-composition analogue, including the argument that for polynomial activations only the multilinear monomial survives (relevant to the power neuron).
   - (e) He et al., 2606.02993 (preprint, June 2026): an energy functional that is the per-neuron group-Fourier diagonal correlation.
   - (f) He et al., 2602.16849: calls cos(w(x+y-j)) the "primary signal" and the rest "noise". Terminology only.
   - (g) Doshi et al., ICLR 2024 workshop: many-term cosine expansion in the style of Gromov.
6. **Harmonic-analysis attribution not confirmed.** The annihilator / Poisson-summation origin is still unconfirmed. Neither Wikipedia page I fetched states the finite-group version, so no bib entry is emitted; none is needed.
7. **Search limits.** WebSearch was exhausted and the Semantic Scholar and arXiv APIs were rate-limited. I searched arxiv.org/search abstract pages through Sept 2026 instead and read the full text of every plausible hit.

**Suggested text:**
- After eq:spectrum: "network-level form of the single-neuron identity of \citet[App.~F.1]{morwani2024feature} and \citet[proof of Lemma~D.7]{li2025nsum}; \citet[App.~F.3]{morwani2024feature} already read the max-margin network's multidimensional DFT on the diagonal."
- Optionally, at the definition of interference: cite tian2025composing, Thm 1.
- Optionally, in the power-neuron appendix: cite marchetti2026sequential, Lemma B.2.

extra_citations.why: Thm 1 and Lemma 1: for a quadratic 2-layer net on an Abelian group, the squared-loss objective is l_k = -2 r_kkk + sum |r_{k1k2k}|^2 + ... The diagonal term r_kkk carries the target correlation (eta(0) up to constants), and a global optimum needs r_kkk = 1 with the off-diagonal terms at 0. This is the squared-loss analogue of the paper's diagonal-mode vs interference split. The arXiv comment reads 'NeurIPS 2025 camera ready', and the PDF header says 39th NeurIPS.

Section 5, Thm 5.1: for modular addition, the initial utility of a quadratic neuron is U = (2/p^3) sum_{k!=0} |xhat[k]|^2 uhat[k] vhat[k] what[k] xhat[k]. That is the per-neuron diagonal-mode correlation at delta=0, the same Fourier computation in a gradient-dynamics setting. The arXiv comment reads 'NeurIPS 2025'.

App. B.1, Lemmas B.1-B.2 give the k-operand, general-group version of the single-neuron identity: sum_g <w,x_{g1..gk}> prod <u_i,x_gi> = |G|^{-1} sum_rho <uhat_1^dagger xhat ... uhat_k^dagger xhat, what^dagger xhat>_rho. For polynomial activations only the monomial k! prod <u_i,x_gi> survives, which is the reduction the paper uses for the power neuron. The arXiv comment reads 'Accepted at ICML 2026'.
